column1: Which authentication method avoids storing API keys for supported Azure AI endpoint calls?
column2:
Managed Identity.
Azure manages the identity's credentials rather than requiring an application-managed API key.
Review source

column1: What financial risk comes from unauthorized AI endpoint calls?
column2:
Unexpected charges from excessive API usage.
Restrict invocation rights and monitor usage.
Review source

column1: What confidentiality risk arises when SQL sends data to an external model endpoint?
column2:
Sensitive database content can leave the database in the request.
Authorize the caller and the external use of the data.
Review source

column1: Why restrict access to an endpoint serving a proprietary fine-tuned model?
column2:
To limit unauthorized probing of the model's behavior.
Endpoint access can expose information about proprietary model capabilities.
Review source

column1: Which transport does sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint require to protect communication?
column2:
HTTPS with TLS encryption.
Encrypted transport does not replace authentication or authorization.
Review source

column1: Where do you enable the logical server's system-assigned identity for Azure SQL outbound calls?
column2:
On the Azure SQL logical server resource's Identity configuration.
Enable it through the Azure portal or a supported Azure management interface.
Review source

column1: Which property identifies the system-assigned identity in a server object returned by Get-AzSqlServer?
column2:
Identity.PrincipalId.
Use Azure resource identity metadata rather than a SQL certificate-store view.
Review source

column1: Whose identity authenticates an Azure SQL REST call using a logical-server Managed Identity credential?
column2:
The logical server's configured managed identity.
The database caller's identity is not automatically forwarded to the AI service.
Review source

column1: Which purpose-built Azure role permits Azure OpenAI inference without permission to manage model deployments?
column2:
Cognitive Services OpenAI User.
Use an inference role rather than granting unnecessary deployment-management rights.
Review source

column1: Which Azure RBAC scope limits an identity's role assignment to one Azure OpenAI resource?
column2:
That Azure OpenAI resource.
A resource-group or subscription assignment can grant access more broadly.
Review source

column1: Which SQL object holds authentication configuration for an external REST call?
column2:
A database-scoped credential.
Pass its name through the REST procedure's @credential parameter.
Review source

column1: Which credential IDENTITY value selects managed-identity authentication for an Azure SQL REST call?
column2:
'Managed Identity'.
The configured identity still needs authorization on the target service.
Review source

column1: What does resourceid specify in a Managed Identity REST credential's SECRET JSON?
column2:
The token's target resource, or audience.
It is not the SQL identity's principal ID or an API key.
Review source

column1: Which resourceid value does the SQL REST example use for Azure OpenAI managed-identity authentication?
column2:
https://cognitiveservices.azure.com
This identifies the token audience, not the deployment's endpoint URL.
Review source

column1: What naming format must a database-scoped credential follow for sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint?
column2:
A valid URL matching the request's scheme, host, and permitted path scope.
A friendly alias such as AzureOpenAICredential does not satisfy these rules.
Review source

column1: Which system stored procedure sends an HTTPS request from supported SQL platforms?
column2:
sys.sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint.
Use it from a stored procedure that controls endpoint access.
Review source

column1: What is the minimum SQL Server version that includes sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint?
column2:
SQL Server 2025 (17.x).
The feature must be enabled on SQL Server 2025 before use.
Review source

column1: Which REST-procedure parameter supplies the endpoint address?
column2:
@url.
This procedure does not require a CREATE EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE object.
Review source

column1: Which REST-procedure parameter selects the database-scoped credential?
column2:
@credential.
Its value must name a credential that satisfies the procedure's URL-matching rules.
Review source

column1: Which T-SQL expression constructs an input JSON object from @InputText?
column2:
JSON_OBJECT('input': @InputText)
A colon separates the JSON key from its value.
Review source

column1: How do you pass a JSON_OBJECT result to a stored procedure's @payload argument?
column2:
Assign it to a local variable, then pass that variable.
Do not put the function call directly in the EXECUTE argument list.
Review source

column1: Which REST-procedure parameter captures the returned response document?
column2:
@response = @response OUTPUT.
The caller's variable must be declared before the call.
Review source

column1: Which T-SQL JSON function extracts an embedding array rather than a scalar value?
column2:
JSON_QUERY.
JSON_VALUE extracts scalars and is not the correct function for an entire embedding array.
Review source

column1: Which JSON path selects the first embedding array in the SQL REST procedure's wrapped Azure OpenAI response?
column2:
$.result.data[0].embedding
The endpoint's JSON body is under result in the SQL response wrapper.
Review source

column1: What does return code 0 mean for sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint?
column2:
The HTTP call completed with a 2xx status code.
Zero is the procedure's return value, not the actual HTTP status code.
Review source

column1: When an endpoint returns HTTP 403, what does sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint return?
column2:
403.
A completed non-2xx response returns its HTTP code rather than automatically throwing an exception.
Review source

column1: Which JSON path holds the actual HTTP status code in the SQL REST response?
column2:
$.response.status.http.code
Read and log this value rather than hard-coding 200.
Review source

column1: How must AI-call logging handle a request that throws before returning an HTTP response?
column2:
Record the failure through an appropriate error-handling path.
An exception can skip the normal post-call logging statement.
Review source

column1: Which statement lets AIFeatureUsers execute dbo.GetEmbedding?
column2:
GRANT EXECUTE ON dbo.GetEmbedding TO AIFeatureUsers;
Underlying REST and credential permissions must also exist in the effective execution context.
Review source

column1: Which statement adds an existing database user app-service-identity to AIFeatureUsers?
column2:
ALTER ROLE AIFeatureUsers ADD MEMBER [app-service-identity];
The database role controls access to the SQL wrapper, not Azure service authorization.
Review source

column1: Which database permission is required for direct REST-procedure calls in Azure SQL Database and Fabric SQL database?
column2:
EXECUTE ANY EXTERNAL ENDPOINT.
Restrict direct invocation rights so callers cannot bypass a controlled wrapper.
Review source

column1: Which permission allows a database principal to use a specific credential for REST invocation?
column2:
REFERENCES on that database-scoped credential.
This is separate from permission to invoke the REST procedure.
Review source

column1: Which auth_mode enables Microsoft Entra token authentication on an Azure Machine Learning managed online endpoint?
column2:
aad_token.
This mode is not supported on Kubernetes online endpoints.
Review source

column1: Which token resource identifies Azure Machine Learning online scoring rather than Azure resource management?
column2:
https://ml.azure.com/
Scoring uses a data-plane token rather than a management.azure.com control-plane token.
Review source

column1: Which RBAC action authorizes scoring on an Azure Machine Learning managed online endpoint with aad_token authentication?
column2:
Microsoft.MachineLearningServices/workspaces/onlineEndpoints/score/action
Grant a role containing this action to the calling identity at the required scope.
Review source

column1: How can Azure SQL invoke an AI service whose hostname is outside the REST procedure's allowlist?
column2:
Expose it through a supported Azure API Management endpoint.
Configure authentication and authorization on both hops.
Review source

column1: Which additional resource needs secured identity-based access in a batch-inference workflow?
column2:
The storage holding the inference data.
Secure storage access as well as access to the endpoint or pipeline.
Review source

column1: What does ORIGINAL_LOGIN() identify in an AI-call log?
column2:
The login that originally established the SQL session.
A shared application login does not identify each human end user.
Review source

column1: Which T-SQL function records the current UTC datetime2 timestamp for an AI call?
column2:
SYSUTCDATETIME().
UTC timestamps support consistent comparisons across environments.
Review source

column1: Which expression measures AI-call duration in milliseconds from @StartTime?
column2:
DATEDIFF(millisecond, @StartTime, SYSUTCDATETIME())
Set @StartTime before the call using the same UTC time basis.
Review source

column1: What can a sudden spike in AI calls from one principal indicate?
column2:
A compromised identity or an application bug.
Alert on unexpected call volumes and investigate the cause.
Review source

column1: Which credential IDENTITY supports API-key headers for an external embedding model in Fabric SQL database?
column2:
HTTPEndpointHeaders.
External model access can use database-scoped credentials rather than workspace roles alone.
Review source

column1: How do Fabric's prebuilt AI models authenticate callers?
column2:
Through Fabric authentication.
This differs from configuring access to your own external Azure OpenAI resource.
Review source

column1: Where is usage of Fabric's prebuilt AI services billed?
column2:
Against Fabric capacity through the Copilot and AI meter.
This is separate from the Spark compute used by a notebook.
Review source

column1: Which app monitors capacity consumption from Fabric's prebuilt AI services?
column2:
The Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app.
Use the Copilot and AI meter to inspect AI-service consumption.
Review source

column1: Who enables Copilot for Fabric SQL database through tenant settings?
column2:
A Fabric tenant administrator.
Workspace membership alone does not enable the feature.
Review source
